items.text: Freelance copywriter seeking advice on portfolio and resume design to attract new clients. Assistant recommended a clean, minimalist layout with strong typography that showcases readability and hierarchy without being flashy. Key advice: use a distinctive but professional font for name/headlines to add personality; keep resume to one page and link to portfolio rather than including samples directly; include 2-3 brief bullet points showcasing measurable results (e.g., "Increased email open rates by 40% for X client") to keep resume scannable while driving traffic to portfolio site.

Workspace setup and wood preparation for resin river tables: For a one-car garage, ensure good ventilation (open doors, fans near windows) and wear a respirator. Maintain workspace at 75-85°F for proper curing. Cover work surfaces with plastic or wax paper and ensure the area is level. For wood preparation: seal the wood first with a thin coat of epoxy or wood sealer to prevent resin from soaking into pores and creating bubbles. Let sealer fully cure, then sand lightly before the main pour. Build a mold using silicone sealant for edges, and plastic pipe or acrylic sheets for mold walls. Plan for 1.5-2 inches depth for the river effect.

Workspace setup and wood preparation for resin river tables: For a one-car garage, ensure good ventilation (open doors, fans near windows) and wear a respirator. Maintain workspace at 75-85°F for proper curing. Cover work surfaces with plastic or wax paper and ensure the area is level. Plan for 1.5-2 inches depth for the river effect.

Workspace setup and wood preparation for resin river tables: For a one-car garage, ensure good ventilation (open doors, fans near windows) and wear a respirator. Workspace setup and wood preparation for resin river tables: For a one-car garage, ensure good ventilation (open doors, fans near windows) and wear a respirator. Maintain workspace at 75-85°F for proper curing. Cover work surfaces with plastic or wax paper and ensure the area is level. For wood preparation: seal the wood first with a thin coat of epoxy or wood sealer to prevent resin from soaking into pores and creating bubbles. Let sealer fully cure, then sand lightly before the main pour. Build a mold using silicone sealant for edges, and plastic pipe or acrylic sheets for mold walls. Plan for 1.5-2 inches depth for the river effect.

For wood preparation: seal the wood first with a thin coat of epoxy or wood sealer to prevent resin from soaking into pores and creating bubbles. Let sealer fully cure, then sand lightly before the main pour. Build a mold using silicone sealant for edges, and plastic pipe or acrylic sheets for mold walls. Plan for 1.5-2 inches depth for the river effect.
